author: 이영빈
prompt: Precision localized sprite-art edit. Edit the supplied existing sprite sheet in-place as a game-ready transparent 4-column by 4-row atlas. Keep every sprite in its original cell, original size, root, exact silhouette, helmet, visor, suit, hands, leg anatomy, footwear, arm gesture and facing. Do NOT mirror any cell or turn a left-facing drawing into a reflected right drawing. These are independent left/right poses, and their empty hands will hold separate right-handed weapon layers in Unity; do not add a gun or wrench into the body art. Main correction ONLY: replace the old exhaust with matching compact white-core, muted pale icy-cyan-edged jet flames. The jetpack has TWO thruster nozzles at its LOWER LEFT and LOWER RIGHT CORNERS. Every flame must visibly join one of these backpack lower corners, never feet, thighs, hips, armpits, center hatch or midair. Respect perspective and body occlusion; two emissions exist physically, but a far plume may be partly hidden, no fake new side-mounted pack. The exhaust axes must be parallel to the character's projected torso/backpack tilt (head-to-pelvis axis); upright body means straight downward jets, tilted body means both jets tilt together, no arbitrary diagonal sideways blast. Remove the displaced old exhaust completely while preserving the actual white thighs and all legs. Keep flames short, narrow, modest, unified texture, grounded in the existing pixel-painted sci-fi style. Actual transparent alpha background, no gridlines, labels, text, drop shadows or new props. Do not restyle, expand helmets, recolor boots or redesign the character.
constraints: Independent left/right art; no body mirroring.
Two outlet lips physically attached to lower backpack corners.
Plumes follow projected torso tilt; rear-view jets can occlude outer thighs.
Existing white-gray outfit, independent hands and separated weapons.
